strengths: Addresses a concrete and important bottleneck in high-resolution and ultra-high-resolution (UHR) optical flow: the quadratic memory and runtime explosion of dense all-pairs correlation volumes in RAFT-like architectures.

The proposed block-sparse correlation volume sampling serves as an exact mathematical drop-in replacement (showing an imperceptible 0.03% EPE difference due to numerical precision) while avoiding the slow recomputations of existing on-demand implementations.

Comprehensive empirical analysis of access patterns and thorough hardware profiling across multiple GPUs (GH200, A100, RTX 4090, RTX 3090), accompanied by clear algorithmic derivations and complexity analysis ($O(P^{1.5})$ space complexity).

Introduces an 8K evaluation benchmark rendered from the photorealistic open-source movie CHARGE with ground truth motion vectors, providing valuable benchmarking for future high-resolution optical flow research.
The simple cascaded inference strategy successfully addresses the degradation in large-displacement estimation at native 8K resolution without requiring architectural retraining.
weaknesses: The speedup is predominantly manifested at high resolutions (4K/8K); at standard benchmark resolutions (e.g., Sintel, KITTI, and Spring in Tables 8-10), the administrative overheads of mask setting and block indexing yield negligible or no runtime improvements over dense tensor operations.
The proposed 8K benchmark dataset comprises only 335 frames from three shots of a single animated movie (CHARGE), which is relatively limited in domain diversity and motion variety.

While memory usage is substantially lower than full precomputation, the block-caching strategy still increases peak memory consumption noticeably relative to purely on-demand sampling (e.g., 17.21 GB vs 10.25 GB for SEA-RAFT at 8K in Table 3).

The cascaded inference technique is fundamentally a standard multi-scale / coarse-to-fine warm-start heuristic; while effective at mitigating large displacement failures, its conceptual novelty is limited.

strengths: Addresses an important and practical bottleneck: scaling dense correlation volume sampling in RAFT-based optical flow architectures to high and ultra-high resolutions (4K/8K), where dense volumes exceed GPU memory and naive on-demand approaches are severely memory-bandwidth constrained.

The proposed block-sparse correlation sampling algorithm is an exact drop-in replacement for RAFT's correlation lookup (showing only 0.03% difference due to floating-point rounding), requiring no retraining or architectural modifications.

Smart system-level design choices, including the patch-major memory layout to maintain 2D spatial locality in block format, masked block sparse matrix-matrix multiplication, and cross-iteration block caching.

Thorough empirical evaluation in isolation across various input dimensions, iteration counts, feature channels, and modern GPU architectures (RTX 3090, RTX 4090, A100, GH200), demonstrating significant memory reductions (up to 95%) and speedups over on-demand implementations.
Introduction of an 8K evaluation benchmark derived from the Blender movie CHARGE, which provides an open testbed for ultra-high-resolution optical flow with rendered ground truth.
weaknesses: Algorithmic novelty is predominantly engineering- and systems-oriented rather than computer vision modeling innovation; the contribution consists mainly of tailoring block-sparse GEMM and caching strategies to RAFT's existing lookup mechanism.

The proposed cascaded inference technique for handling large motion at 8K resolution is essentially a heuristic coarse-to-fine warm-start scheme, which is standard practice in classical and deep optical flow literature.

Non-compute bookkeeping overheads (mask generation, index gathering, cache updating) represent a significant portion of execution time (e.g., ~72% at 1024px and ~35% at 4096px according to Table 1), rendering the method ineffective at improving throughput on standard lower-resolution datasets (e.g., 0% speedup on standard Sintel and KITTI resolutions).

The newly introduced 8K CHARGE benchmark is modest in scale and diversity (3 sequences, 335 frames from a single computer-animated movie, forward flow only), limiting its ability to represent varied real-world ultra-high-resolution capture conditions.

strengths: Addresses an important and practical bottleneck in optical flow: the quadratic memory and computational footprint of all-pairs correlation volumes in RAFT-like architectures, which prevents processing ultra-high-resolution (4K/8K) images.

The proposed block-sparse correlation volume sampling algorithm is mathematically exact (near 0% numerical deviation from baseline RAFT) while achieving sub-quadratic space complexity O(P^1.5) via patch-major layout, block-level mask generation, and inter-iteration block caching.

Comprehensive isolated benchmark across multiple modern hardware architectures (GH200, A100, RTX 4090, RTX 3090), demonstrating up to 90% speedups over RAFT's default on-demand CUDA sampler and up to 95% memory reduction compared to the full 4D correlation volume.

Introduction of an 8K ground-truth optical flow evaluation benchmark based on the Blender movie 'Charge', providing an insightful analysis of failure modes (e.g., large motion breakdown at native high resolutions).
The simple cascaded inference extension for SEA-RAFT successfully resolves the large displacement degradation at high resolution without requiring any retraining or architectural modifications.
weaknesses: The benchmark dataset is relatively small in diversity, containing only 3 sequences (335 frames / 332 pairs) from a single Blender project and evaluating only forward flow.

The cascaded inference strategy is essentially a standard coarse-to-fine multi-scale warm-start heuristic; while practically effective, its technical novelty is limited and somewhat disconnected from the core operator optimization.

As shown in the runtime breakdown (Table 1), non-compute overheads (setting masks, computing block indices, cache maintenance) consume a substantial fraction of the total execution time (over 50% at 1024px width), indicating that deeper low-level kernel fusion is still needed for optimal efficiency at moderate resolutions.

The operator specifically targets local recurrent lookup architectures (RAFT, CCMR, SEA-RAFT) and does not directly extend to global matching/transformer architectures (such as GMFlow) that require dense global cross-attention matrices.
